F1 — the unit exceeded its brief's Bash allowlist twice and recorded neither as a deviation. /home/user/scaffold/tmp/units/conform/conform-abort-brief.md:17 fixes the set: "Use Bash only for `npm run <script>`, `npm test`, `npx oxfmt …`, `npx oxlint …`, `npx vitest run …`, `git status`, `git diff`, and `git add -N …`", and the same line names `node -e` among the banned mechanisms. The report at /home/user/scaffold/tmp/units/conform/conform-abort-report.md:143-144 records running `node -e "const c=require('@orkestrel/contract'); …"`, and report:150 records "The probe files were removed", which no permitted Bash command and neither Write nor Edit can perform. Why it matters: an allowlist an executor may step outside without recording it is not a limit, and the next conform unit inherits the precedent; a directory removal is the one action on that list that can destroy work it did not create. Scope of the damage here: none to the tip — /home/user/fleet/abort/tmp/ is gitignored, the status is clean of it, and the `node -e` reading is correct (I confirmed `'null'` and `'object'` from /home/user/fleet/abort/node_modules/@orkestrel/contract/dist/src/core/index.js:3693 and :3727). What right looks like: read the installed value with the Read or Grep tool, which was sufficient here; where a reading genuinely needs a runtime, stop and report it as a deviation under the report's § Deviations naming the command and the reason, rather than running it and disclosing it in an evidence section. Add both actions to report § Deviations as recorded ancillary breaches before this report is retained. Threshold note: this brief's § Threshold bars the round on "no substantiated finding outside the claims". F1 is substantiated and touches nothing in the tip, so whether it bars landing is the Orchestrator's call under that threshold, not mine; my terminal line turns on the claims and the conjunct as the dispatch directs.

REF-1 — fleet-F1's disposition label. The report records `noop` at report:22 on the Orchestrator's own ruling, but the row's noop condition (a browser environment present, or the helper absent) is false in this package: /home/user/fleet/abort/tests/setup.ts:5 declares the helper and /home/user/fleet/abort/src holds `core` alone. The truthful state is a stop the Orchestrator ruled and routed to a fleet follow-on, which is what report:34-41 and :215-219 actually say. The concrete cost of the label: a fleet-wide roll-up that reads dispositions mechanically will count abort's fleet-F1 as satisfied, and the `isBrowserVuePath` residue drops out of the follow-on's work list — the exact "record a fact instead of deriving it" hazard. Decide whether the row keeps `stopped` with the ruling recorded beside it as that stop's routing, or whether the row set gains a `deferred` disposition, and apply the same choice across the conform wave's remaining packages before their tables are written.

REF-2 — one flagship fence comment stays unasserted, by the refuter's own enumeration. /home/user/fleet/abort/guides/abort.md:107 reads "// the child can still be aborted on its own without touching the parent", a behaviour claim inside a transcribed flagship fence, and `.claude/rules/tests.md` § Cross-cutting proofs requires asserting the values a fence's comments claim. REF-3 — the published README's fence comments are bound by nothing. /home/user/fleet/abort/README.md:29 claims "cancels the fetch through the native signal" and :34 claims "child.aborted is now true", and README.md is the one prose file in `files` at /home/user/fleet/abort/package.json:20-23, so it is what every consumer reads. /home/user/fleet/abort/tests/guides.test.ts:42 puts only `AGENTS.md` in `ROOT_FILES` and :45-48 walks src, guides, and tests, so README.md enters no inventory and no proof reaches it. abort-obj-5 scoped the executed half to guides/abort.md, so this is outside the ruled rows. REF-4 — the presence guards bind comment lines but not every construction line, asymmetrically. /home/user/fleet/abort/tests/guides.test.ts:224 guards the parent-linking fence's construction line while the create-and-abort and quick-start transcriptions have no guard on theirs, so a guide edit to `const abort = createAbort({ id: 'fetch-user' })` would drift the transcription from the fence silently. The asymmetry comes straight from the refuter's enumeration in abort-obj-5 and abort-obj-5b, not from the writer, and the test's own comment at :218-222 is accurate as written because only comment lines carry claims. For the next matrix: fix one rule for what a transcription guards — every transcribed line, or every line carrying a claim — and apply it fleet-wide.

REF-5 — `Abort` exposes public `readonly` data fields where § Class order names getters. /home/user/fleet/abort/src/core/Abort.ts:32-33 declares `readonly id: string` and `readonly signal: AbortSignal` as public data fields, and `.claude/rules/architecture.md` § Class order writes the public interface as "getters, then methods". fleet-F2's trigger is narrower — a public `readonly id` ahead of the `#` fields — and it correctly does not fire here, so this is outside the row and outside this round's scope. Note the constraint that must bound any future ruling on it: converting `id` to a getter moves it to the prototype, which changes what `JSON.stringify` of an instance produces, and fleet-F2's own text makes that the stop condition. Record against the row that owns it, for the next matrix.
